battery.guidance: Never dispose of batteries in general household bins! Take to an authorized e-waste drop-off box or battery collection depot to prevent toxic lithium/acid leakage.

biological.guidance: Place in the green organic/wet bin. Ideal for home composting or municipal biomethanation processing.

brown-glass.guidance: Rinse thoroughly, remove metal caps, and place in the dry recyclables blue bin for color-separated glass recycling.

cardboard.guidance: Flatten boxes to save space. Keep dry and free of food oil or grease before depositing in the recyclables bin.

clothes.guidance: If in wearable condition, donate to local charities or shelters. Torn garments can be deposited in municipal textile recycling banks.

green-glass.guidance: Rinse clean and discard in designated glass recycling stream. 100% infinitely recyclable.

metal.guidance: Empty and rinse aluminum cans or food tins. Crush cans if possible to optimize bin volume.

paper.guidance: Keep clean and dry. Avoid recycling paper contaminated with food residue, wax, or chemical adhesives.

plastic.guidance: Rinse bottles and containers. Check recycling triangle (#1 PET, #2 HDPE are widely recyclable). Replace caps securely.

shoes.guidance: Tie pairs together by laces. Donate usable pairs or take to shoe recycling programs that shred soles into playground turf.

trash.guidance: Non-recyclable household waste destined for sanitary landfill or waste-to-energy incineration. Segregate strictly to avoid contaminating recyclables.

white-glass.guidance: Rinse clean. Clear flint glass is highly valuable for remelting into new food containers and glass jars.
